title: Add optional auto-stash behavior for deploy when working tree is dirty
specification:
# PRD: Add optional auto-stash behavior for deploy when working tree is dirty

Priority: medium

## Problem
Deploy currently fails whenever the repo working tree is not clean, which blocks operators from deploying `dev` to `main` when local tracked or untracked changes are present.

## Goal
Allow deploy to proceed from a dirty working tree by automatically stashing local changes before the deploy flow and restoring them afterward, with explicit status and failure handling.

## Requirements
- Add an explicit deploy option or config-controlled behavior for auto-stash; do not silently change deploy semantics without an operator-visible setting.
- Stash both tracked and untracked changes before deploy begins.
- Run the existing deploy flow against the clean repo state after stashing.
- Attempt to restore the stash after deploy completes or fails.
- Surface clear status messages for stash created, deploy started, deploy succeeded/failed, and stash restore succeeded/failed.
- Define failure behavior for stash restore conflicts so the operator is warned and recovery instructions are available.
- Add focused automated coverage for clean-tree deploy, dirty-tree deploy with auto-stash enabled, untracked-file handling, deploy failure with restore, and restore-conflict scenarios.

## Acceptance Criteria
- When auto-stash is disabled or unset, dirty-tree deploy still fails with the current clean-tree error.
- When auto-stash is enabled and the tree is dirty, deploy stashes local changes, completes the normal deploy flow, and restores the stash afterward.
- Untracked files are preserved across the deploy flow.
- If deploy fails after stashing, the system still attempts restoration and reports the final restore outcome.
- If stash restoration conflicts, the deploy result includes explicit conflict/restoration status instead of claiming a clean success.
- Tests cover the new control path and regressions around existing clean-tree deploy behavior.

## Verification
- Run the current implementation check: `npm run typecheck`.
- Run targeted deploy coverage, especially [tests/smoke/deploy.test.ts](/Users/macmini/Documents/GitHub/autonomy-v2/tests/smoke/deploy.test.ts) and any related unit tests.
- Manually verify one clean-tree deploy and one dirty-tree deploy with auto-stash enabled in a disposable repo state.

tasks.title: Add optional deploy auto-stash flow with restore status and deploy coverage
tasks.description: Update the deploy command and supporting git/deploy helpers so deploy can optionally proceed from a dirty working tree by stashing tracked and untracked changes before the existing `dev` to `main` promotion flow, then attempting to restore the stash afterward on both success and failure paths. Add an operator-visible control surface for the behavior through an explicit deploy option and/or existing repo config plumbing, preserve the current dirty-tree failure when auto-stash is disabled or unset, and surface clear status and recovery messaging for stash creation, deploy start/result, stash restore result, and restore conflicts. Likely touch points include `src/autonomy-v2/commands/` deploy and git operation paths plus targeted coverage in `tests/smoke/deploy.test.ts` and any supporting unit tests around deploy or git helpers.
acceptance: Deploy exposes an explicit operator-visible auto-stash control through the CLI and/or existing config path, and dirty-tree deploy behavior remains unchanged when that control is disabled or unset.

When auto-stash is enabled and the working tree is dirty, deploy stashes both tracked and untracked changes before the normal clean-tree deploy flow runs, then attempts to restore the stash after deploy completion regardless of whether deploy succeeds or fails.

Deploy status output clearly reports stash creation, deploy start, deploy success or failure, stash restore success or failure, and any restore-conflict condition without claiming a clean success when restoration is incomplete or conflicted.
Restore-conflict handling leaves the operator with explicit warning and actionable recovery instructions that identify the stash restoration problem and the next manual recovery step.

Automated coverage verifies current clean-tree deploy behavior, dirty-tree deploy with auto-stash enabled, untracked-file preservation, deploy failure followed by restore attempt, and stash restore conflict reporting, with targeted updates centered on `tests/smoke/deploy.test.ts` and any related unit tests.

Verification for the completed task includes `npm run typecheck` and the relevant targeted deploy test suite, plus a disposable manual check of one clean-tree deploy and one dirty-tree deploy with auto-stash enabled.
